summary: Ignis Line turns NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspots into one harmonized monthly record of satellite-detected fire activity, July 2002 to November 2026, for any 0.5-degree map cell, country, continent, the world or a custom area. MODIS and VIIRS differ in sensitivity and overpass time, satellites join and leave, and Aqua's orbit has drifted, so raw hotspot counts cannot be compared across years. We treat each satellite (Aqua MODIS, S-NPP VIIRS, NOAA-20 VIIRS) as a witness: we convert each to the Aqua scale with calibrated ratios, combine them with an uncertainty estimate, and compare every month with the same calendar month of 2003-2022. Each area and month gets a verdict (above, within or below normal, or "cannot determine") with probabilities and an evidence panel. The web app has a map, a historical calendar, "% of normal", CSV export, and a methods page that publishes every validation result, including the 18 tests that failed.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Ignis Line is a web platform and a published data record that separates real changes in satellite-detected fire activity from changes caused by the sensors. It covers July 2002 to November 2026 and can be explored for any 0.5-degree map cell, country, continent, the world, or a custom rectangle or polygon. Every area and month gets a verdict (above normal, within normal, below normal, cannot determine, or no detected activity), a 90% interval, the probabilities behind the verdict, and an evidence panel that names the satellites used and the caveats. A hotspot is a satellite detection, not a fire count or burned area, and the tool says so everywhere.

HOW IT WORKS

1. We download the NASA FIRMS active-fire archives (MODIS, S-NPP VIIRS, NOAA-20 VIIRS, 2002-2025) and the 2026 near-real-time and standard data, and grid them to fire-active cell-days per 0.5-degree cell and month.

2. Each satellite is a "witness". VIIRS is converted to the Aqua MODIS scale with ratios calibrated on the overlap years, per fire region, day or night and season, with partial pooling (stratum, GFED fire region, global).

3. The witnesses are combined by a precision-weighted mean with an uncertainty that grows when they disagree. Aqua night data are excluded from May 2024 because of orbit drift.

4. Each month is compared with the same calendar month of 2003-2022 (25th, 50th and 75th percentiles). A verdict is given only when the data support it with at least 80% probability; otherwise the tool says "cannot determine".

5. One function, harmonize_area(), computes every area (preset and custom), so conversion errors that are shared inside a calibration group are never summed as if independent.

WHAT IS IN THE APP

A map with verdicts and an optional satellite imagery view, a month picker and time-lapse, a historical calendar (years by months, % of normal or activity), a per-satellite chart, an evidence panel, a ranked anomaly list, an analytics tab (raw versus harmonized by year, season profile, rank, coverage, compare), five featured stories with verified numbers, CSV export, India's official boundary on the map, and a Methods and validation page.

HONESTY AND VALIDATION

We pre-registered a validation suite (the "Witness Stand") before seeing results, and we published every result, including failures: 38 entries, 18 PASS, 18 FAIL, 2 INCONCLUSIVE. The record passes the tests on satellite-change steps (B1), known artifacts such as outages and drift (B3), cross-satellite agreement (C1), data gaps (D2) and leaving one region out (E1). It fails the two-independent-paths test on big fire events (A1: the converted S-NPP estimate is 58% to 80% of Aqua in the peak months of the four decided events), the planted-jump detection (B2), and the savanna control (CTRL). Interval coverage is 82% pooled but below 80% for night values and for about half of the regions. We found that the Aqua/VIIRS ratio rises with activity (saturation), built an activity-dependent v0.2 conversion, and did not adopt it because it did not meet our pre-registered rule. We keep the failures visible so users know where not to trust the record: extreme months are likely under-converted, cell-level verdicts are often "cannot determine", and intervals can be too narrow at night.

TOOLS

Python 3.13 (DuckDB, pandas, NumPy, PyArrow) for the pipeline and the validation suite; FastAPI for a read-only API over Parquet products stored with Git LFS; React, TypeScript, Vite, MapLibre GL, deck.gl and Apache ECharts for the app; pytest, Vitest and ruff for tests. Every number shown in the app is checked against the products by a checker (more than 6.4 million values checked, 0 mismatches).

IMPACT AND WHO IT IS FOR

Emergency managers can ask whether a month is abnormal for a place, land managers whether the regime is changing, scientists how much of a trend is the sensor, and journalists whether burning changed or only the observation did. The challenge asked for a burning-activity calendar that joins MODIS's long history with VIIRS's detail, comparison with the historical median, and CSV export; all three are in the app.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

Treating each satellite as a witness whose testimony is weighed by what it could actually see, saying "cannot determine" when the evidence is insufficient, and publishing the tests the method fails.

MODIS/Aqua MYD14 V061 active fire detections (standard, via FIRMS)
VIIRS/NPP (S-NPP) VNP14IMG V002 375 m active fire detections (standard)
VIIRS/JPSS1 (NOAA-20) VJ114IMG V002 375 m active fire detections (standard)
MODIS MCD14DL near-real-time active fire detections (FIRMS NRT)
VIIRS S-NPP VNP14IMGT near-real-time active fire detections (FIRMS NRT)
VIIRS NOAA-20 VJ114IMGT near-real-time active fire detections (FIRMS NRT)
NASA GIBS imagery (Blue Marble and Aqua true colour), optional map background
projectRefs: Natural Earth admin-0 countries, India point of view, 1:10m v5.1.1 (map country boundaries; public domain)
GFED4s basis regions (14 fire regions; van der Werf et al. 2017, ESSD 9, 697-720), used to pool calibration
MapLibre GL JS (open-source map rendering library)
deck.gl and Apache ECharts (open-source map layers and charts)
DuckDB, FastAPI and React (open-source data engine, API framework and UI library)
